## Appearance

Josephine Barry is an elderly woman with wrinkled cheeks and sharp, twinkling black eyes. She has a thin, prim, and rigid appearance.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077), [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne’s Life P17](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0017), [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne’s Life P31](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0031), [v1 CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Queen’s P8](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0008)_

## Personality

Josephine Barry is characterized as a particularly prim and proper woman who is prone to scolding dreadfully. She is also considered rather selfish, historically showing little care for anyone other than herself.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P54](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0054), [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne’s Life P31](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0031)_

## History

Josephine Barry, the aunt of Diana's father, lived in [Charlottetown](../codex/places.md#charlottetown). During a stay at [Orchard Slope](../codex/places.md#orchard-slope), she was startled when [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) accidentally leaped onto her bed late at night. Although initially furious and threatening to cut off Diana's music lessons, Miss Barry was charmed by Anne's honest confession, leading her to forgive [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md), extend her stay in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), and become close friends with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md).

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P27](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0027), [v1 CHAPTER XIX. ## Quotes

> "I dare say your claim to sympathy is just as strong as mine. It all depends on the way we look at it. Sit down here and tell me about yourself."
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P88](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0088)

> "Remember, you Anne-girl, when you come to town you’re to visit me and I’ll put you in my very sparest spare-room bed to sleep."
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P96](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0096)

> "Oh, I must, hey? I rather think Diana did her share of the jumping at least. Such carryings on in a respectable house!"
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P82](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0082)

> "She amuses me, and at my time of life an amusing person is a rarity."
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P92](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0092)

> "I’ve made up my mind to stay simply for the sake of getting better acquainted with that Anne-girl,"
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P92](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0092)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--josephine-barry.md)

Josephine Barry and [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) are firm friends who frequently visit and amuse one another. They first met when [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) accidentally jumped onto Miss Barry while she was sleeping in a guest bed, causing great offense. After [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) personally visited her to confess and explain her actions, Miss Barry was charmed by Anne's honesty, leading to a close friendship and invitations to visit her in the city.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P27](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0027), [v1 CHAPTER XIX. ### [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/diana-barry--josephine-barry.md)

[Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) is the grand-niece of Josephine Barry. Their relationship faced brief strain when [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) and [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) startled Miss Barry by jumping on her bed, which led Miss Barry to threaten to cancel Diana's music lessons before [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) successfully intervened.
